question: A 27-year-old man comes to the physician for a follow-up examination. Paroxetine therapy was initiated 6 weeks ago for a major depressive episode. He now feels much better and says he is delighted with his newfound energy. He gets around 8 hours of sleep nightly. His appetite has increased. Last year, he had two episodes of depressed mood, insomnia, and low energy during which he had interrupted his job training and stopped going to the gym. Now, he has been able to resume his job at a local bank. He also goes to the gym three times a week to work out and enjoys reading books again. His temperature is 36.5°C (97.7°F), pulse is 70/min, and blood pressure is 128/66 mm Hg. Physical and neurologic examinations show no abnormalities. On mental status examination, he describes his mood as ""good.” Which of the following is the most appropriate next step in management?"?

options.opb: Switch from paroxetine to venlafaxine therapy
options.ope:
Switch from paroxetine to lithium therapy
"

analysis: The patient is showing significant improvement in his depressive symptoms with paroxetine therapy. He has regained his energy, appetite, and is able to resume work and activities he enjoys. There are no signs of abnormalities on physical and neurologic examinations. Given the positive response to paroxetine and the absence of any concerning symptoms, it would be appropriate to continue the current therapy.
